comments.body:
=== SESSION: e369 Jira DC — every child closed, 4 harness rounds, 6 -> 3 live failures ===

--- OUTCOME ---
ALL 15 children closed: the 8 stories (J1-J8) were already closed; the 7 open bugs
(3fe5, 1a9f, 37e7, 39c1, 9bb9, 18a5, 5200) closed this session, plus 339a, discovered
and fixed within it. The epic's own 13 ACs are under independent verification.

--- THE HARNESS ARC, one pinned DC 8.17.1 image ---
  30857265932  collected=58   6 failed / 51 passed / 1 xfailed   (baseline)
  30867072561  collected=58   5 failed / 52 passed / 1 xfailed
  30874380112  collected=61   4 failed / 56 passed / 1 xfailed
  30880394880  collected=61   3 failed / 57 passed / 1 xfailed   (final)

COVERAGE ROSE 58 -> 61 WHILE FAILURES FELL 6 -> 3, with `skipped` pinned at exactly 1
(the canary) in every run. The direction of those two numbers together is the claim;
either alone is gameable.

The 3 remaining reds are ONE measured platform limitation — DC will not move or clear a
SUB-TASK's `fields.parent` — recorded in docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md with evidence ids.

--- MERGED (14) ---
  1330 37e7 clear Epic Link, not sub-task parent      1341 39c1 pass-level epic parent cell
  1331 465d transport split 799 -> 230, five mixins   1342 9bb9 epic-parent idempotence cell
  1332 3fe5 pin the harness project template          1343 339a stop re-pushing a removed parent
  1333 259b record what the pinned DC image does      1345 18a5 shape priority and assignee
  1337 1a9f verify the sub-task parent write          1346 1a9f assert the refusal live
  1340 18a5 translate the create payload              1348 18a5 drop null optionals, wrap parent

--- 339a: A DEAD FEATURE WITH A GREEN SUITE ---
88d9's inbound parent-clear was UNREACHABLE in any bidirectional pass. The outbound differ
re-pushed the parent in the same pass and inbound discarded its own clear as a contradiction;
the clear's precondition and the re-push's precondition are IDENTICAL, so it could never fire.

Why the 88d9 suite stayed green: every cell passes `outbound_mutations=None`, and the ONE cell
supplying outbound context HAND-BUILDS the entry and asserts the suppression as desired. That is
a real oracle asserting the wrong thing because its input was fabricated — a step beyond a
vacuous double, and the more dangerous shape.

Found only because 37e7's rewrite finally reached its precondition and failed somewhere new.

--- 18a5: THREE LAYERS, EACH HIDDEN BY THE ONE ABOVE ---
A single 400 aborts the whole create, so each fix revealed the next:
  1. bridge-schema NAMES  ticket_type/title/status posted as Jira field ids
  2. value SHAPES         priority and assignee sent bare; Jira REST wants objects
  3. NULLS + parent key   assignee arrives as None (drop it); parent wraps {"key":…} not {"name":…}
Seventh instance of "Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — and the first where
the seam was missed for names AND shapes AND nulls.

--- METHOD, THE PART WORTH CARRYING ---
1. I CLOSED 39c1 ON THE WRONG EVIDENCE and reopened it. AC1 demanded a PASS-LEVEL assertion;
   I ticked it from a cell that calls `set_parent` directly. Hours earlier I had refused to tick
   that same AC from the capability map for exactly that reason, then collapsed the distinction
   one step later. Adjacent-green substitution is not a thing you learn once.
2. HELD-OUT TDD KEEPS PAYING. On 3fe5 and 18a5 the held-out cells caught what the visible ones
   could not. On 1a9f the implementer resolved a conflict IN PRODUCTION CODE by treating an
   absent read-back field as "no evidence" — defensible in the abstract, but it existed only to
   satisfy a double that does not model state. Making the doubles faithful instead exposed a
   SECOND stale double the first fix would have masked.
3. A FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION THAT COULD NOT BE TESTED IS NOT A REFUTATION. The 339a trace predicted
   a `RECON: outbound_update` breadcrumb. It was absent from the CI log — and so were ALL `RECON:`
   lines, because the harness captures pass stderr into `cp.stderr` and prints it only on
   assertion. Inconclusive, not negative. The local test then produced it directly.
4. TWO SUBAGENTS REPORTED CONTRADICTIONS RATHER THAN MASSAGING THEM: one that its brief predicted
   the wrong casualty, one that the mechanism refuted its own starting hypothesis. Both were right.

--- INFRASTRUCTURE FOUND ALONG THE WAY ---
* [rebar:94d0-5d19-2d06-4fa7] LIVE CREDENTIALS in a ticket COMMENT (129e) blocked every
  tickets-branch push for ~8h, stranding 122 commits. Push protection held — the secrets never
  reached GitHub — but the store reported success to every writer while diverging from the
  remote. The silent auto-push failure is arguably the worse defect. Operator resolved.
* A review-bot maintenance window produced a fail-closed LLM-Review -1 whose signature is
  indistinguishable from a permissions regression; I filed it as a defect and the operator
  corrected me. Recorded because the inference was well-formed and still wrong.
* `d2ce: default local dev to Bedrock` landed mid-session, so the completion verifier began
  resolving to Bedrock and closes failed until `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]` was installed —
  fixed properly rather than bypassed with --force-close.

comments.body:
=== PART 2: the close was REVERSED, and the reason changes how this epic must finish ===

The epic was closed, then reopened on the operator's rule that closing without completion
verification is prohibited. Debugging the Bedrock error proved that rule right for a reason
nobody had seen: **the verification behind the earlier PASS was blind.**

    same command, same ticket, same instance — only the max_tokens clamp differs
    BEFORE  128 provider 400s, 32 of 32 epic-bug-screen calls FAILED  ->  verdict PASS
    AFTER     0 provider 400s,  0 failures                            ->  verdict FAIL (exit 1)

--- THREE ROOT CAUSES, each explaining distinct symptoms ---
 1. **max_tokens is never re-clamped.** `max_output_cfg` only ever RAISES, so a cap set for the
    128K verifier rides into a call resolving to the 64K trivial model. Anthropic tolerated it;
    Bedrock rejects it, so `d2ce` (default local dev to Bedrock) surfaced it. FIXED — Gerrit 1361,
    clamped at `build_model_settings` where the model is known and the 400 originates, applied
    only to models the ceiling table knows (clamping an UNMAPPED model to the 16000 fallback would
    shrink a deliberate operator floor — a worse regression than the bug).
 2. **The screen degrades open.** `epic_bug_screen._row` turns a failed screen into "unrelated".
    Defensible per candidate; when all 32 fail it silently makes the caused_by bug floor a no-op
    with NO aggregate signal. RECORDED, NOT FIXED — the remedy changes when an epic close blocks,
    which is an operator ruling.
 3. **The missing attestation was INTENDED.** `certifiable = not uncertified` — two uncertified
    descendants withheld the signature, documented at the line. **My original framing of ticket
    1019 as a "fail-open gate" was WRONG and is corrected on that ticket.**

--- WHAT THE GATE SAYS NOW THAT IT CAN SEE ---
FAIL, on two legitimate findings: AC4 has no real attestation (my independent AC verification pass
flagged the identical gap separately — two independent checks agreeing), and open bug 2e47 indicts
the subtree. 2e47 is the capability map's own output and was invisible for as long as the screen
was blind.

--- STATE HANDED OVER ---
 * epic e369: **in_progress, claimed**, 45 descendants, 6 open, **0 uncertified**
 * 0059 + 2bc7 REOPENED — they were the two uncertified closes; re-close each on its OWN merits
 * 94d0 CLOSED — credentials rotated + history scrubbed (operator-attested); the two systemic
   items carried forward to 2a76, not dropped
 * Gerrit open: 1361 (max_tokens fix, LLM-Review +1), 1359 (the probe)

--- METHOD FINDINGS, PART 2 ---
 1. **I closed 39c1 on the wrong evidence and reopened it.** AC1 demanded a PASS-LEVEL assertion; I
    ticked it from a cell that calls `set_parent` directly — having refused that exact substitution
    hours earlier. Wrote the real cell; it passed live. Adjacent-green substitution is not a thing
    you learn once.
 2. **An investigation that refutes its own hypothesis is worth more than one that confirms it.**
    The 37e7 trace killed its own peer-evidence theory and found 339a instead — a defect that made
    88d9's parent-clear unreachable in ANY bidirectional pass while its unit suite stayed green,
    because the one outbound-aware cell FABRICATED its input.
 3. **A prediction you cannot test is not a refutation.** The 339a trace predicted a `RECON:`
    breadcrumb. It was absent from CI — and so were ALL `RECON:` lines, because the harness captures
    pass stderr and prints it only on assertion. Inconclusive, not negative.
 4. **Two subagents reported contradictions instead of massaging them** — one that my brief
    predicted the wrong casualty, one that the mechanism refuted its own premise. Both were right.
 5. **Gates caught two of my own process misses**: a 289-line change with no `file_impact` +
    plan-review (bugfix-size-attestation), and a new workflow unregistered in the locked naming
    table. Both correct findings; the sequence was mine to get right.
 6. **A new `workflow_dispatch` workflow cannot be dispatched until it lands on the DEFAULT branch**
    — unlike a harness run, which reuses an already-landed workflow on a topic branch.
